$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

 

And the product rule is

$$
\frac{\text{d}(u\cdot v)}{\text{d}x}={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)
$$

Using the product rule, chain rule, and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={(7\sqrt{x})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arsinh}⁡{e}^{x}+7\sqrt{x}\cdot (\operatorname{arsinh}⁡{e}^{x})^{′} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{x}}\cdot \text{arsinh}\,({e}^{x})+7\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{({e}^{x})}^{2}+1}}\cdot {({e}^{x})}^{′} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{x}}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡{e}^{x}+7\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}+1}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{x}}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡{e}^{x}+\frac{7{e}^{x}\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2x}+1}}\end{aligned}
$$
